The mission

Ride. Explore. Return.

The route is intentionally simple: stay on NH44, spend the best part of the morning at Penukonda, eat clean, and protect the return window.

300–330 kmEstimated total ride
~150–165 kmOne-way from Hebbal
10:00 AMTarget Penukonda arrival
5:30 PMPreferred home arrival
⚠️

Weather is the variable tomorrow

The current outlook indicates increasing thunderstorm/rain risk around Penukonda and Rayalaseema later in the day. The itinerary therefore front-loads the destination: reach around 10 AM, finish sightseeing by 11:45 AM and begin the return around 12:45 PM. If lightning, heavy rain or strong wind develops, stop at a proper facility rather than pushing through.

Recommended route

Hebbal → Yelahanka → Devanahalli → Chikkaballapur → Bagepalli → Kodikonda → Penukonda → Penukonda Fort

Return via the same NH44 corridor. Avoid unnecessary backroad detours tomorrow: the goal is a great ride with a reliable return buffer.

Destination

Penukonda Fort

Once associated with the Vijayanagara Empire, Penukonda gives the ride a proper heritage payoff.

“Don't just ride 300 km to take two photos. Make the destination part of the story.”

Your 10:00–11:45 AM window is enough to experience the main heritage points without compromising the weather and return plan.

⛽ Fuel strategy

Start FULL. Around 300–330 km is manageable, but don't depend on theoretical range. If either bike approaches half-tank during the day, top up at a reliable fuel station. Around Penukonda, refuel before the return if needed.

Pre-ride

10-minute departure checklist

✓ Full fuel tank
✓ Tyre pressure
✓ Chain condition / lubrication
✓ Front & rear brakes
✓ Headlight / indicators / brake light
✓ Phone + mount + charging
✓ Rain jacket / waterproof layer
✓ Licence / RC / insurance / PUC
✓ Water + basic snacks
✓ Helmet, gloves & riding gear
🏍️

Ride smart, not fast

Lead/follow can alternate, but the ride should stay at a comfortable shared pace. Wet roads, reduced visibility, crosswinds and highway traffic matter more than the Duke's extra performance. If conditions turn bad, stop safely and reassess.
